extracted.intended_audience: authors, editors, peer reviewers, and systematic reviewers in biomedical and health-research fields
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards relevant to transparent reporting of clinical trials and health research, and methods to detect, assess, and adjust for publication and reporting bias in systematic reviews and meta-analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: ICMJE uniform requirements for manuscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: Uniform requirements for manuscripts submitted to biomedical journals: writing and editing for biomedical publication (International Council of Medical Journal Editors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets standard expectations for manuscript preparation and disclosure for biomedical journals (referenced as a core standard for submission). URL provided in reference list (http://www.icmje.org/).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of reporting guidelines / EQUATOR Network
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines for reporting health research: the EQUATOR network’s survey of guideline authors; helping editors, peer reviewers and authors improve the clarity, completeness and transparency of reporting health research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages use of established reporting guidelines (e.g., CONSORT, PRISMA) to improve clarity, completeness and transparency of research reports; cited as a tool for editors/reviewers/authors to enhance reporting quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical trial registration requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles for international registration of protocol information and results from human trials of health related interventions (Ottawa statement) and analysis of trial registration at ClinicalTrials.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trial registration of protocol information and results is promoted to prevent biased under-reporting and selective outcome reporting; registration should be required by editors and registering agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global trial bank / beyond registration (complete public reporting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals for a global trial bank for clinical trial reporting and for making protocol information and results publicly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calls for systems beyond mere registration (e.g., global trial bank) to facilitate comprehensive public reporting of trial results and reduce selective non-reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preventing selective reporting / withholding unfavourable results
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence and warnings about withholding unfavourable results in drug company sponsored clinical trials and selective reporting in clinical trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policies and editorial practices should discourage suppression of unfavourable findings; transparency and mandatory reporting are emphasized to prevent biased evidence bases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest disclosure and management
rubrics_metrics.description: Conflict of interest disclosure policies and practices in peer-reviewed biomedical journals and discussions of the effects of disclosing conflicts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals should have clear disclosure policies; awareness of potential perverse effects of disclosure is noted (disclosure alone may have unintended consequences).

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial peer review quality and practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Effects of editorial peer review, including randomized trials of blinding reviewers and asking them to sign reports, and assessments of blind vs unmasked review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer review practices (e.g., blinding reviewers, signed reports) influence review quality; evidence-based editorial policies should guide peer review design to improve manuscript assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access and accessibility of research
rubrics_metrics.description: Arguments and evidence about open access to research results and whether open access articles have greater citation impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open access is promoted to increase accessibility and possibly impact of research; policymakers and funders increasingly support open access to research outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive literature searching including unpublished and grey literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Importance of searching for unpublished studies, ongoing trials, regulatory (e.g., FDA) sources, conference abstracts, handsearching and contacting authors to identify unpublished evidence for systematic reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systematic reviewers should use a broad search strategy (databases, registries, handsearching, internet searches, contacting authors, regulatory sources) to reduce publication and language bias and capture 'buried' trials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessing risk of bias in included studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessing risk of bias in included studies as outlined in the Cochrane Handbook for systematic reviews of interventions (chapter referenced).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Risk-of-bias assessment is an essential component of systematic reviews; use standard tools and Cochrane guidance to evaluate selection, performance, detection, attrition, reporting bias, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funnel plots for detecting publication bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of funnel plots (including contour-enhanced funnel plots) to detect asymmetry in meta-analyses that may indicate publication bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funnel plots are a visual diagnostic but have limitations (asymmetry may arise from heterogeneity or chance); contour-enhanced plots can help distinguish publication bias from other causes of asymmetry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rank-correlation test for publication bias (Begg & Mazumdar)
rubrics_metrics.description: Operating characteristics of a rank correlation test for publication bias (Begg & Mazumdar).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statistical test based on rank correlation between effect estimates and their variances; useful as one component of assessing funnel-plot asymmetry but with known limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regression-based tests for small-study effects (Egger/related methods)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regression-based methods to detect small-study effects or funnel plot asymmetry (e.g., Egger test and related regression approaches).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regression tests provide an analytic assessment of asymmetry but may be inappropriate in some situations (e.g., few studies, heterogeneity); interpret alongside other evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modified tests for binary outcomes / small-study effects (Harbord test, Rucker arcsine test)
rubrics_metrics.description: Modified tests designed for small-study effects in meta-analyses with binary endpoints (Harbord RM et al.; Rucker G et al. arcsine test).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use tests tailored to the data type (binary outcomes) when standard asymmetry tests are unsuitable; be aware of type I error inflation in some tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trim-and-fill method (Duval & Tweedie) for adjusting meta-analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Trim and fill: a funnel-plot-based method of testing for and adjusting for publication bias in meta-analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trim-and-fill imputes missing studies to estimate adjusted effect; useful as sensitivity analysis but can be misleading in presence of heterogeneity and other violations—interpret cautiously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fail-safe N and file-drawer approaches (Orwin, Rosenberg, others)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fail-safe N calculations and other methods for estimating how many missing studies would be required to change meta-analytic conclusions (file-drawer problem).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fail-safe N offers a measure of robustness but has limitations; complementary modeling and sensitivity analyses are recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection models and sensitivity analyses for publication bias (Vevea & Hedges; Copas; others)
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection models and sensitivity analyses that model the publication/selection process to assess and adjust for publication bias (general linear models, selection/weight functions, Copas methods).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model-based approaches can adjust for publication bias under explicit assumptions; they require careful implementation and sensitivity analyses because results depend on model choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regression-based adjustment and simulation approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of regression-based methods to adjust for publication bias and comprehensive simulation studies evaluating methods (e.g., Moreno et al., Peters et al.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regression-based and simulation-evaluated methods can provide adjusted estimates or evaluate method performance; use as part of a broader assessment rather than sole proof of bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excess significance test (Ioannidis & Trikalinos)
rubrics_metrics.description: An exploratory test for an excess of significant findings in a body of literature indicating potential bias toward positive results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can flag possible selective reporting or bias when too many 'positive' studies are present relative to expected; interpret alongside methodological quality and heterogeneity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphical and statistical cautions and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Empirical findings that visual identification of publication bias is often unreliable and that many statistical tests have limitations (e.g., misleading funnel plots, low power, type I error inflation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine multiple approaches (visual, statistical tests, search for unpublished data, trial registries, sensitivity analyses) and interpret results cautiously, considering heterogeneity and small-study effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparing large trials vs meta-analyses / update and monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparisons of results from large, simple randomized trials versus meta-analyses of smaller trials and the need for updating systematic reviews (how conclusions change when reviews are updated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systematic reviewers should consider evidence from large trials and ensure reviews are updated; discordance between large trials and meta-analyses warrants investigation of biases and heterogeneity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of regulatory and non-traditional sources to reduce bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of unpublished trials via regulatory agencies (e.g., FDA), trial registries, and other non-journal sources as important for comprehensive reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include regulatory databases and other non-indexed sources where possible to capture unpublished or suppressed trial data that could affect conclusions.
